subject: Novalyft: request for elevated uptime + operational runbook handoff
messages:
From: Lauren Cho <lauren@novalyft.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novalyft.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Uptime ask for enterprise contract - 99.99% + p95 latency

Hi Sofia,

Thank you again for the demo yesterday — the infra looks promising. Our execs are pushing for a firmer operational commitment before legal will sign: they want a 99.99% monthly uptime commitment and a p95 inference latency target of <120ms for our production traffic pattern.

We understand this is above your standard public SLA and expect there may be carveouts. Can you share whether Redwood can make this commitment for Novalyft (we're looking at a Dedicated footprint), what operational controls you require, and a draft SLA we can review? We attached our minimal procurement checklist to the RFP.

Timeline is tight: procurement review next Thursday (2026-12-17). Appreciate any quick guidance and a draft we can circulate to legal.

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Sourcing Manager | Novalyft
lauren@novalyft.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Cho <lauren@novalyft.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Uptime ask for enterprise contract - 99.99% + p95 latency

Looping you all in — Novalyft is asking for 99.99% monthly uptime and p95 <120ms on Dedicated. Procurement needs a draft SLA by 2026-12-17.

Primary questions for ops/engineering:
- Can Dedicated support a contractual 99.99% (monthly) guarantee? If not, what mitigations (hot standby, cross-region failover, manual intervention windows) would make Legal comfortable?
- Is the p95 <120ms realistic for their projected QPS and sequence lengths? If we need a scoped commitment (e.g., for pinned model vX and request size distributions), what boundaries should we set?

Marcus — can you assess feasibility + runbook needs? Karthik — can you confirm what we should put in SLA about model pinning / fallbacks? Evelyn — need guidance on wording (carveouts, credits, maintenance windows).

I'll draft a response + draft SLA once I have operational inputs.

— Sofia
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Cho <lauren@novalyft.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Uptime ask for enterprise contract - 99.99% + p95 latency

Quick ops readout (high level):
- 99.99% (~4.3 minutes/month downtime) for Dedicated is possible but requires a small, retained hot pool + cross-region failover + SLA-specific runbook. We'll need explicit constraints (region, maintenance windows, allowed planned downtime) and the customer must accept an operational playbook and on-call escalation path.
- p95 <120ms: depends heavily on model, sequence length, and whether they're okay with cold-KV-cache misses counting as latency exceptions. For typical gpt-like models at 8k context and mixed QPS, 120ms is aggressive unless they agree to: (a) pin a quantized variant, (b) accept prewarmed endpoints, and (c) allow a fallback to a slightly higher-latency compatible model for spike protection.

Attachments: I put together a draft runbook and an operational checklist (novalyft-uptime-runbook.pdf). Key asks from our side:
- Dedicated cluster reservation (min capacity commit)
- Proactive load forecasts 2 weeks out
- Right to trigger transparent throttling for overload with agreed fallback model mapping

If Legal wants hard credits for any breach we should define blame boundaries (redwood infra vs customer misuse / traffic shaping). Happy to run a short tech deep-dive with Novalyft next week.

— Marcus
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Lauren Cho <lauren@novalyft.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Uptime ask for enterprise contract - 99.99% + p95 latency

Operational + product considerations:
- Model pinning: recommend we commit to a specific model version (e.g., redwood-alpha-1.3) and define a compatibility window for rollouts. Any model upgrade would be agreed via a change-control clause with a 30-day notice.
- Fallback behavior: propose an explicit fallback map: primary -> compatible-quantized model (same accuracy tier) with documented performance delta; declare that fallbacks triggered by overload do not count as SLA violations as long as latency remains within a higher agreed threshold (e.g., p95 <200ms) and customer accepts fallback semantics.
- Telemetry: include token-level latency histograms and sampled traces in the monthly SLA report. We can provide integration with their monitoring (Datadog) for 6 months during ramp.

Suggested wording for the SLA draft: "Commitment applies to requests routed to the Dedicated cluster configured and reserved for Customer and for the pinned model version(s). Exemptions: scheduled maintenance, force majeure, client-side misconfiguration, traffic that exceeds committed capacity, and fallback activations as defined in Appendix A."

I can annotate the draft SLA with these specifics. Marcus — want me to include the fallback map table in the runbook?

— Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Cho <lauren@novalyft.com>, Procurement <procurement@novalyft.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 18:30:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Draft SLA + next steps for Novalyft Dedicated commitment

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the patience — please find a single draft attached (Novalyft_SLA_Draft_v2.docx) and an operational runbook (novalyft-uptime-runbook.pdf). Highlights / constraints:
- Uptime commitment: 99.99% monthly for requests routed to Novalyft's reserved Dedicated cluster (Region: us-west-2), excluding scheduled maintenance windows (we propose 02:00-04:00 PT weekly), force majeure, and traffic above committed capacity.
- Latency commitment: p95 <120ms for pinned model redwood-alpha-1.3 under committed capacity profile (detailed in Appendix B). Fallback activations (primary->compatible-quantized) are defined in Appendix A; fallbacks are not SLA breaches provided latency remains below agreed fallback threshold (p95 <200ms).
- Operational requirements: reserved capacity, 2-week forecasting cadence, shared Datadog read-only view for 6 months, and a signed runbook with escalation contacts.
- Remedies: service credits tiered by monthly impact. Legal language on credits and dispute windows is in the draft but open to redlines.

Next steps I propose:
1) Novalyft legal/procurement to review the attached draft by 2026-12-23.
2) If acceptable, schedule a 30–45 minute ops alignment call (Marcus + Karthik + Novalyft SREs) during the week of Dec 27.
3) Sign runbook and commit to capacity by Jan 7, 2027 to meet Jan onboarding.

If you want, we can also scope a short performance-validation run (2–3 days of controlled load) prior to the go-live to baseline p95 latency.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

— Sofia
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
